info.bio:
Taylor Alison Swift (Reading, Pennsylvania, 13 de diciembre de 1989) es una cantante y compositora de música country y pop estadounidense. Trabajaba con la compañía discográfica independiente Big Machine Records desde 2006 hasta 2018, año en el que se unio a Republic Records donde se encuentra hasta la actualidad. Taylor Swift hizo su aparición en las listas de country con su sencillo Tim McGraw.

Su primer álbum Taylor Swift fue lanzado al mercado a finales de 2006, y ha sido catalogado desde entonces como 7X Multi-Platinum por el RIAA.

podcast.title: Album Sales (2009)
podcast.body: Taylor Swift's album sold 3.2 million copies in 2009, making it one of the top sellers of that year. Her performance provided a slight uplift in sales figures after a period of continuous decline, but the overall trend of diminishing album sales persisted. "2009, with Taylor Swift with 3.2 million."

podcast.title: Suitcase Transportation Rumor (2017)
podcast.body: In the summer of 2017, paparazzi photographed two men carefully carrying a large, bulky suitcase out of Taylor Swift's New York apartment. A website captioned the image suggesting Swift was being transported inside the suitcase from her Tribeca apartment into a truck, with nearly a dozen security guards present to move the package discreetly, as she had been unseen for an extended period. "Taylor Swift being transported in a huge suitcase from her Tribeca apartment into her truck in the trunk."

podcast.body: The November 2022 incident involving Taylor Swift concert tickets highlighted the severe impact of ticket buying bots. Millions of fans simultaneously attempted to purchase tickets for 52 stadium shows, but they were overwhelmingly outcompeted by millions of bots, leading to widespread frustration and demonstrating the bots' superior speed and efficiency. podcast.title: Current Popularity vs. Historical Ubiquity
podcast.body: Taylor Swift is acknowledged as an absolutely huge artist, capable of playing to 50,000 to 60,000 people a night. However, her impact is contrasted with the historical ubiquity of bands like the Rolling Stones or Led Zeppelin, suggesting that while she has massive fans, she doesn't command the same level of universal cultural consensus that older bands did. "Taylor Swift is huge, absolutely huge, but she is not as huge as bands used to be back in the day."

podcast.title: Discography Withdrawal and Return
podcast.body: Taylor Swift famously removed her entire discography from Spotify due to dissatisfaction with the platform. However, approximately a couple of months before November/December 2017, she reversed this decision, granting Spotify her full discography "prácticamente gratis sin condiciones" for immediate upload. "Hace poco hace apenas un par de meses se arrepentía y le daba prácticamente gratis sin condiciones toda su discografía para que la subiese cuanto antes."

podcast.body: Taylor Swift made expert use of social media applications to engage her fanbase, creating a sense of intimacy through her posts that mirrored the conversational style of her songs. An example of her engaging with other artists includes a 2014 Instagram video selfie where she lip-synced Kendrick Lamar's "Backseat Freestyle," which was widely shared. "Taylor Swift was making expert use of the social apps to stoke fan engagement, projecting intimacy through social posts that mirrored the conversational tone of her hits."

podcast.body: Taylor Swift's vinyl records, despite being top sellers, are considered unlikely to retain significant value long-term because her audience is not typically composed of demanding collectors, and such artists' albums often end up in bargain bins for a dollar 15-20 years later. "tienes a Taylor Swift [...] el tipo de público que tienen estos artistas no es de coleccionista, no es de compradorexigente por cómo he evolucionado la historia de la música, este tipo de artistas tienden a acabar en las tanquetas 15, 20 años después de todo a un dólar."

podcast.title: Impact on Popularity and Accessibility
podcast.body: Swift's decision to remove her music led to a significant drop in her popularity, listenership, and even video views on YouTube, as it complicated access for her audience, particularly her young fanbase (aged 17-20). Her record label ultimately recommended that she return to Spotify to regain momentum. "Teglor suy tenía el problema de que su popularidad escuchas, incluso las visitas de sus videoclips en un YouTube caían bastante tras su retirada en Spotify. Y veía cómo se caía bastante, dejaba estar a pide candelero por culpa de no tener en Spotify y de poner complicados sus oyentes en el acceso a su música."

podcast.title: Mainstream Reach Comparison
podcast.body: Taylor Swift's mainstream appeal is used as a comparative example to illustrate how the concept of "mainstream" has changed. It's suggested that if she existed in 1995, her music would be inescapable daily, making it easy for anyone to name multiple singles. However, in the fragmented post-2000 music landscape, only her dedicated fans ("swifties") would easily recall three singles, demonstrating how even major stars now inhabit a more niche role within a diverse music culture. "If this were 1995, Taylor would have been way more popular than she is today and everyone. I mean, everyone would have been exposed to her music daily. So answering that question, naming three singles, would have been very easy."

podcast.title: Multiple Imperial Phases
podcast.body: Taylor Swift has experienced at least two distinct imperial phases. Her first fully imperial phase peaked in 2014-2015, marked by her pivot from country to pop. After a dip in the late 2010s due to controversy, she achieved a remarkable post-pandemic comeback in the 2020s, arguably becoming even more imperial. "So yes, for certain megastars, multiple Imperial phases are possible, and certain phases are more legendary than others."

podcast.title: Second Chance Hits - General Mention
podcast.body: Taylor Swift is among the artists who have experienced "second chance hits" or "bringbacks," where singles initially flopped or did nothing on the charts before a catalyst propelled them to smash success. "Everyone from the Beatles to Prince, Guns and Roses to Taylor Swift has had one of these so-called bringbacks."

podcast.title: Unofficial Mascot of Corinthians Soccer Team
podcast.body: Taylor Swift serves as the unofficial mascot for the Brazilian soccer team Corinthians, based in Sao Paulo, due to a phenomenon known as the "Taylor Swift rule." Since 2006, the team has never lost a game whenever she releases an album. Conversely, the team consistently loses immediately after Paul McCartney releases a new record. "Going back to 2006, the team has never lost a game when Tate releases an album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unparalleled Career Control
podcast.body: Taylor Swift is recognized for her exceptional control over every aspect of her career, from her music creation to complex behind-the-scenes business dealings. "Few people are in charge of the careers as much as Taylor Swift. She directs everything she does from the music she makes to all kinds of behind-the-scenes business dealings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Use of Pre-recorded Bits in Shows
podcast.body: Taylor Swift has been observed incorporating pre-recorded elements into her live performances, a practice that led to public mockery from bands like the Foo Fighters. This situation highlights the ongoing debate within the music industry and among fans regarding the balance between production spectacle and authentic live musicianship. "Remember when they poke fun at Taylor Swift for using pre-recorded bits and her shows?"

xref.title: Dan Wilson's Songwriting Prowess
xref.body: Guitarist and singer Dan Wilson has achieved considerable recognition as a highly sought-after professional songwriter. He co-wrote Adele's massive global hit "Someone Like You," which topped charts in dozens of countries and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year. He also received a Grammy for his production work on Adele's "21" album and was nominated for a Grammy for writing "Not Ready to Make Nice" for the Dixie Chicks. His extensive songwriting credits include collaborations with dozens of other notable acts, such as Fantagram, John Legend, Steve Perry, Josh Groban, Jason Barraiz, Leanne Rhyme, Stevie Nick's Halsey Cold War Kids, K-Flay, Weezer, Panic at the Disco, and Taylor Swift. "But the big story here is guitarist and singer Dan Wilson. He's become a renowned songwriter for hire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mocking Taylor Swift for Backing Tracks
xref.body: The Foo Fighters openly mocked Taylor Swift for her use of pre-recorded elements in her live shows. At their London Stadium concert in June 2024, they called their tour "the Errors Tour," explaining, "We've had more than a few eras and even more than a few effing errors. That's because we actually play live," directly implying a contrast with artists like Swift who rely on backing tracks. "Remember when they poke fun at Taylor Swift for using pre-recorded bits and her shows?"

xref.title: Successful Songwriting Career
xref.body: After his success with Semisonic, Dan Wilson has had a highly lucrative career as a songwriter, earning "real money." He penned at least six songs for The Dixie Chicks (including a Grammy winner for Song of the Year), three songs for Adele's *21* album (including "Someone Like You"), and co-written with numerous other major artists such as Taylor Swift, Tom Morello, Celine Dion, John Legend, and Pink. "But it is as a songwriter where Dan has made the real money."
